correctness.rationale: The first pivot is exactly a comparison of one half-normal diagonal entry with n-1 independent planar Gaussian l^p norms. Polar integration gives an exact angular tail. Four isolated nondegenerate minimizing directions yield the stated Laplace constants for p<2 and p>2, whereas p=2 has the exact exponential tail. A separately reconstructed chi-square extreme-value transfer integral produces the gamma prefactor and logarithmic exponent; a uniform Taylor expansion about p=2 yields the binary-entropy crossover. All hypotheses, p=1/2/infinity boundaries and first-column normalization are explicit. The standalone script passed 34 finite deterministic assertions, which corroborate rather than prove the asymptotic limits.

value.rationale: Numerical GEPP implementations genuinely use different coordinate norms to compare complex entries, as documented by the 2026 primary article. The result resolves the entire natural p-family at leading order, identifies a qualitatively different universal p>2 asymptotic, the singular Hilbert logarithm, a nonconstant critical window, and the threshold separating below-uniform and above-uniform initial no-swap probabilities. These parameter-space boundaries and sharp constants are structurally informative, not an arbitrary finite experiment or a routine endpoint substitution.
